Registered Office Address vs Service Address in the UK: What’s the Difference?

A comprehensive legal breakdown for non-resident directors on address privacy, Companies House public records, statutory mail handling, and virtual office compliance.

ADVAQ Legal Team
7 Min Read · Published July 2026
Companies Act 2006 Address Rules
Key Takeaways (TL;DR)
Registered Office Address

Applies to the COMPANY. Must be a physical address in the UK. Receives official government mail from Companies House & HMRC. Visible on public register.

Directors' Service Address

Applies to the INDIVIDUAL DIRECTOR / PSC. Can be located anywhere in the world, but using a UK virtual address hides your home address from public records.

  1. 1. What is a UK Registered Office Address?

1. What is a UK Registered Office Address?

Under Section 86 of the Companies Act 2006, every UK Limited Company must at all times have an official Registered Office Address situated in the jurisdiction of incorporation (England & Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland).

This address acts as the official legal headquarters of your company. It is where statutory communications, legal notices, court summons, and official letters from UK authorities (Companies House, HMRC, ICO) are delivered.

Key Rules for Registered Office Addresses:

  • Must be a physical street location in the UK (PO Boxes are forbidden).
  • Is permanently displayed on the public Companies House online register.
  • Must be located in the same UK home jurisdiction as the company's registration.

2. What is a Directors' Service Address?

While the Registered Office belongs to the company, a Service Address belongs to the individual human beings managing the company — specifically directors, secretaries, and People with Significant Control (PSCs).

The Service Address is the official correspondence address for a director where official mail concerning their directorship is sent.

Crucially, Companies House requires every director to provide both their Usual Residential Address (URA) and a Service Address. The Service Address is published on the public record, while your residential address is kept in a secure, non-public database accessible only to credit reference agencies and law enforcement.

4. Why Overseas Directors Must Protect Personal Home Privacy

If a non-resident director registers their personal home address overseas as their Service Address, that address becomes permanently searchable on the internet via Companies House databases and third-party company information aggregators (such as Endole, Duedil, and Google Search).

Spam & Cold Mail Harassment: Marketing companies harvest public Companies House records daily to send unwanted physical junk mail and cold solicitations.
Identity Theft & Security Risks: Publishing your home location alongside your full legal name and month of birth exposes you to identity fraud.
